assessment.overall_rationale: The replicates contain three strongly conserved programs—xenobiotic conjugation, peroxisomal lipid oxidation, and sulfur/nitrogen metabolism—with only modest differences in scope and emphasis.

pair_scores.rationale: Both modules describe the same Phase I/II hepatic oxidation and conjugation program for xenobiotics, steroids, and bile acids with concordant enzyme roles and excretory output.

The modules intersect through hepatic oxidative metabolism and aldehyde detoxification, but fatty-acid catabolism and lipid-droplet handling are peripheral to the left module's conjugative xenobiotic program.
Bile-acid coupling and general hepatic metabolic homeostasis provide context, but cysteine and nitrogen disposal use distinct central mechanisms from xenobiotic oxidation and conjugation.
ER lipid processing, Cyb5b, and sterol export connect the modules, but lipid storage and fatty-acid oxidation differ centrally from xenobiotic and steroid conjugation.
Both modules encode essentially the same coordinated lipid-droplet, peroxisomal fatty-acid oxidation, lipid-aldehyde clearance, and peroxisomal quality-control mechanism.
They share only broad hepatic metabolic-stress context and a peripheral Sord association, while their substrates, machinery, and physiological outputs differ.
Taurine-dependent bile-acid conjugation links sulfur metabolism indirectly to bile-acid detoxification, but the asserted enzymatic mechanisms and disposal products are different.
Both concern hepatic catabolic homeostasis and oxidative by-product management, but amino-acid nitrogen disposal is mechanistically distinct from peroxisomal fatty-acid oxidation.

Both center on Cdo1-driven cysteine catabolism and taurine production while incorporating Agmat, Car5a, G6pc, and Insr connections to nitrogen disposal and metabolic control, with the right module placing greater emphasis on sulfur homeostasis.
